body:
- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

Provides a default `<C-e>` mapping for `picker.history()` picker based on the one described in https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/discussions/1926#discussioncomment-14032617 . It only works for entries that are either a command or a search. For all other entries, the picker is kept open and the mapping does nothing.

 --- Neovim history picker
 ---
---- Pick from output of |:history|.
+--- Pick from output of |:history|. Use `<C-e>` to edit current match in cmdline.
 --- Notes:
 --- - Has no preview.
 --- - Choosing action depends on scope:
 ---     - For "cmd" / ":" scopes, the command is executed.
 ---     - For "search" / "/" / "?" scopes, search is redone.
 ---     - For other scopes nothing is done (but chosen item is still returned).
+--- - `<C-e>` only works for "cmd" / ":" / "search" / "/" / "?" scopes. It does
+---   nothing for all other scopes.

comment_data.body:
No need for screenshot testing here. Just testing that command line is empty and the picker is still active should be enough.

If it doesn't *have to* be screenshot testing or it is possible to have a reasonably same coverage by alternative concise code, don't do screenshot testing. Adding new screenshot comes with extra disk usage. Albeit small, should be avoided if reasonable.

+    local cur_match = MiniPick.get_picker_matches().current

comment_data.body:
1. If validate function is used only in a single case, define it locally. It makes it easier to parse the test. Usually name it `validate`.
2. No need to return a value if it won't be used later.
3. Probably, can also fit an extra check whether picker is active or not.
4. Can have extra step inside it to ensure clean state, i.e. ensure that picker is closed (`type_keys('<C-c>')`).
